claims.statement: For the governed two-use half-skew BSSC, fix W and X^2 to four symbols and the four deterministic product-code orientations (U,V)=(X^2,0),(2X_1,X_2),(X_2,2X_1),(0,X^2), and vary only the 16 positive masses q(W,X^2). At the tensor product of the exact one-use RTD optimizer, whose 4x4 mass matrix has entries (11-sqrt(105))/120, 1/30, and (11+sqrt(105))/120 in the displayed symmetry pattern, the half-weight Marton functional L_{1/2} has constant gradient and a negative-definite Hessian on the full 15-dimensional simplex tangent space. A standard-library checker works exactly in Q(sqrt(105)), verifies all 15 gradient log-product identities, and gives an exact LDL^T decomposition with 15 strictly negative pivots and exact reconstruction. Hence this tensor point is a strict local maximum in the stated fixed-map quotient; its value is 2 L_RTD, and every distinct sufficiently close law in this quotient has selected-law Marton value below 2 L_RTD because min(E_Y,E_Z) <= L_{1/2}. This local theorem does not rule out distant points, directions activating other (W,U,V,X^2) atoms, stochastic or different maps, larger auxiliaries, a two-letter Marton gain in another architecture, Marton additivity, or a capacity converse.

program/multiletter-marton-achievability.title: Multiletter Marton achievability
program/multiletter-marton-achievability.objective: Determine whether finite-letter Marton coding can improve half-skew BSSC achievable sum rates and rigorously characterize structural restrictions on candidate multiletter witnesses.

program/multiletter-marton-achievability.title: Finite-auxiliary Marton foundations and RTD threshold
program/multiletter-marton-achievability.summary: Develop finite-auxiliary multiletter Marton normalization, superadditive-limit foundations, and rigorously certified randomized-time-division comparison thresholds within their exact conditional scope.
conditions: The capacity lower bound and resulting Fekete-limit lower bound are conditional on the explicitly stated hypothesis (H-Marton).
The one-letter identity with randomized time division is conditional on the explicitly stated hypothesis (H-binary).

item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.title: Finite-super-symbol, superadditivity, and RTD calculus proof
item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.summary: Proof used to establish the linked accepted claim. It bounds each finite-auxiliary Marton functional by binary output entropies, concatenates independent finite laws using the minimum-term inequality to prove superadditivity, applies Fekete's lemma, and proves exact scaling for repeated selected laws. Under (H-Marton), it converts an epsilon-optimal finite law into a finite super-channel Marton rate pair and flattens the resulting code to the original channel. Separately, receiver-skew symmetrization reduces randomized time division to a scalar difference curve, whose derivative identifies q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30 and yields the accepted closed form. The proof preserves all stated conditional hypotheses and does not establish a fixed-blocklength capacity converse.

item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.title: Finite-auxiliary Marton multiletter foundation and directed RTD threshold
item/marton-multiletter-finite-foundatio.summary:
Accepted statement:

For the governed half-skew BSSC P and every n >= 1, define M_n^fin(P) as the supremum of the displayed private-message Marton functional over finite auxiliary alphabets U,V,W and finite laws (U,V,W)-X^n-(Y^n,Z^n). Unconditionally, 0 <= M_n^fin(P) <= 2n, M_{m+n}^fin(P) >= M_m^fin(P)+M_n^fin(P), and Fekete's lemma gives lim_n M_n^fin(P)/n = sup_n M_n^fin(P)/n; k independent copies of a selected n-letter law of value S_n have value exactly k S_n. Assume (H-Marton), the exact finite-DMBC private-message Marton achievability theorem stated in the README. Then C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n for every n and hence C_sum(P) is at least the displayed Fekete limit. For the exact BSSC randomized-time-division value L_RTD, the README's symmetrization and calculus proof gives the stated closed form at q_-=(15-sqrt(105))/30, and the directed standard-library certificate proves the strict intervals 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028007 < L_RTD < 0.3616428844219546156634415781505870072079810107238605552037137298028008 and 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056014 < 2 L_RTD < 0.7232857688439092313268831563011740144159620214477211104074274596056016. Assume additionally (H-binary), the exact binary-input Marton-equals-randomized-time-division theorem stated in the README; then M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD. Under (H-Marton), a selected finite n-letter law strictly improves the governed RTD achievable lower bound through super-symbol normalization iff S_n > n L_RTD; under both hypotheses this is equivalently a strict improvement over the complete one-letter Marton sum optimum. This append-only claim repairs only the finite-auxiliary scope, conditional super-symbol conclusion, conditional one-letter identification, and decimal certification of transaction f6ea30479b9ca461294ba89a8a1a31c06ce59d08; that transaction is a corrective/provenance reference rather than a mathematical premise. No fixed-n equality is a capacity converse.

Scope qualifications (verbatim):
- The capacity lower bound C_sum(P) >= M_n^fin(P)/n and the resulting Fekete-limit lower bound are conditional on (H-Marton).
- The identity M_1^fin(P)=L_RTD is conditional on (H-binary).
- Equivalence between improvement over RTD and improvement over the complete one-letter Marton optimum requires both (H-Marton) and (H-binary).
- All optimizations defining M_n^fin(P) are restricted to finite auxiliary alphabets; no optimizer or cardinality theorem is assumed.
- No fixed-n equality is asserted or used as a capacity converse.
- The declared transaction is corrective/provenance material only and is not a mathematical dependency.

item/marton-rtd-directed-interval-certif.title: Directed RTD threshold interval certificate
item/marton-rtd-directed-interval-certif.summary: Computation used for the certified numerical portion of the linked accepted claim. It brackets sqrt(105) by exact rational square comparisons, propagates directed 120-digit decimal intervals through the accepted closed form for L_RTD, expands correctly rounded logarithms outward, and verifies that the resulting enclosures lie strictly inside the stated intervals for L_RTD and 2L_RTD. It certifies only those intervals and the associated finite-scope structural audit; it does not prove (H-Marton), (H-binary), or any capacity converse.
